question.value: Is circumstellar CO detectable around a metal-poor globular cluster AGB star (47 Tuc V3), and what do its wind velocity and CO strength say about the wind-driving mechanism and the ISRF?

evidence.quote: We report the first detection of circumstellar CO in a globular cluster.
ALMA (project code 2016.1.00078.S) observed 47 Tuc V3 in Band 7
observed 47 Tuc V3 in Band 7 on 2018 May 12, 13 and 15

evidence.quote: The remaining windows were observed at a resolution of 15.625 MHz ($\sim$13.5 km s$^{-1}$)
The CO $J$=3–2 line (345.796 GHz) was covered at a resolution of 488 kHz
The $uv$-coverage of the array is sensitive to angular resolutions between 1.14 and 5.51$^{\prime\prime}$.

findings_qualitative.value: CO line is about an order of magnitude weaker than for Galactic stars with similar mass loss, consistent with ISRF photodissociation

evidence.quote: We retrieve a CO line intensity an order of magnitude lower than this.

findings_qualitative.value: SiO line is asymmetric and brighter, likely a maser

evidence.quote: suggesting the line is more likely masing

claims.hypothesis: Circumstellar CO can be detected in CO J=3-2 around a globular cluster AGB star
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 7 observations of 47 Tuc V3
claims.result: CO detected at 7 sigma, v_LSR –40.6 km/s
claims.finding: First detection of circumstellar CO in a globular cluster

evidence.quote: The CO line is detected at 7$\sigma$ at a rest velocity $v_{\rm LSR}$ = –40.6 km s$^{-1}$

claims.hypothesis: The wind terminal velocity is set by radiation pressure on dust
claims.experiment: Compared v_inf with Galactic stars and the sqrt(Z) law
claims.result: v_inf is 2–3x slower than Galactic stars, matching 0.2 Zsun

evidence.quote: the wind is likely to be driven by radiation pressure on dust

claims.hypothesis: Strong ISRF photodissociates CO in globular clusters
claims.experiment: Compared CO intensity with Galactic stars and the MZL+15 model
claims.result: CO an order of magnitude weaker; matches model prediction

evidence.quote: its strength confirms a model that includes CO dissociation by the strong interstellar radiation field present inside globular clusters

why_this_data.value: V3 chosen as farthest from cluster centre, hence least subject to ionising radiation; higher CO transitions excited closer to the star

evidence.quote: We selected the third-brightest AGB star, V3, for re-observation, as it is the furthest from the cluster centre

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Magnetic fields cannot be completely ruled out as the wind driver

evidence.quote: Magnetic fields cannot be completely ruled out either

limitations_admitted.value: Single object; possible geometric asymmetries or time dependence

evidence.quote: it is difficult to ascertain with certainty the wind-driving mechanism in metal-poor stars from observations of a single object

referee_caveats_inferred: Only a 3.8 sigma peak and one star; the metallicity scaling rests on one object
Galactic comparison stars are poorly matched in type and properties
Parabolic fit has reduced chi^2 of 2.2 and the 1.5 sigma redshifted wing is unresolved
SiO maser interpretation is not tested

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA project code given and data acknowledged via ADS/JAO.ALMA

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00078.S.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-50 GB raw for 5.2 h in Band 7
reproducibility.score_reason: Data are public and the measurements are simple, but calibration and imaging settings are not given.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Imaging and calibration recipe is largely unstated, so the line fluxes are only approximately reproducible.

companion_papers.why: Previous ALMA CO J=2-1 non-detection and ISRF/CO dissociation model
